name: Daniel
charge: Purposing in his heart not to defile himself with the king's meat; praying three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem, decree or no decree
summary: A captive boy in Babylon refused the king's meat and wine and asked for pulse and water; ten days later he looked better than the rest. Sixty years later, an old man under Darius, he kept his windows open and prayed as before, knowing the den was signed. He was in the den one night and the God he served shut the lions' mouths.
offense: Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself with the king's portion. He requested an alternative and proposed a ten-day trial, answering the officer's fear without abandoning his purpose (Daniel 1:8-16). Service in a foreign court did not require surrender of his obligations to God. Under Darius, his enemies could find no fault in his administration and sought occasion against him through the law of his God. After learning that the decree against petitioning any other than the king was signed, Daniel continued kneeling, praying, and giving thanks three times daily toward Jerusalem, as before (Daniel 6:4-10). The threat did not create his devotion, and it did not stop it.
judgment: God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs. At the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat. God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams. My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian. Ezekiel names him with Noah and Job; Gabriel calls him greatly beloved.

entries.commentary: In the third year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it, and the Most High gave Jehoiakim into his hand with part of the vessels of the house of God. Nebuchadnezzar carried those vessels into the land of Shinar to the house of his god and put them in his treasure house. This came to pass exactly as the prophets had warned. -

The king commanded to bring certain of the children of Israel, of the king's seed and of the princes: young men without blemish, well favoured, skilful in all wisdom, cunning in knowledge, understanding science, and able to stand in the king's palace. They took the best and the most educated among us, taught them the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans, and set them to build up their kingdom. It is the same thing today, where our people serve in the governments and the congresses and are used to build up a system that is not our own. Often those who are chosen are not loyal to their own people; they are assimilated to believe they are a part of the system and accepted by that society, and they are well rewarded for it. When our people were carried over in the dark ages they were a civilized, educated people, engineers and men of every profession, and they were used to serve and build up Babylon. Israel is the greatest nation the earth has known, and Babylon benefited off our wisdom and our knowledge. The king also appointed them a daily provision of the king's meat and of the wine which he drank.

Among those taken were of the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. The prince of the eunuchs gave them new names, Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, part of assimilating them into the king's service.

It pleased Darius to set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom, with three presidents over them, of whom Daniel was first, so the king should have no damage. Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm. He was set in a very high position in government.

The presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom but could find none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was found in him. He was blameless. This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in. They concluded they could only find something against him concerning the law of his God. -

The presidents and princes assembled and persuaded Darius to sign a firm decree that whoever asked a petition of any god or man for thirty days, save the king, would be cast into the den of lions, by the unchanging law of the Medes and Persians.

When Daniel knew the writing was signed he went home, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem kneeled and prayed three times a day, giving thanks as he did before. The men assembled, found him praying, and reported to the king that Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, regarded neither the king nor the decree but made his petition three times a day. They really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God.

The king was displeased with himself and laboured till sundown to deliver Daniel, but the men pressed that the law could not be changed, so he commanded Daniel cast into the den, saying, thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee. The king already understood why he was under the realm of Babylon and had seen what was going on. A stone was laid on the den and sealed with the king's signet.

The king went to his palace and passed the night fasting, with no instruments of music brought before him and his sleep gone from him. Why would the king be fasting. He rose very early and went in haste to the den, crying with a lamentable voice, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God able to deliver thee from the lions.

Daniel answered that his God had sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths because innocency was found in him and he had done no hurt. The king was glad and commanded Daniel taken up, and no manner of hurt was found on him because he believed in his God; then the accusers, their children, and wives were cast in and the lions brake their bones before they reached the bottom. -

Darius wrote to all people, nations, and languages that in every dominion men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God, stedfast for ever, whose kingdom shall not be destroyed and who delivereth and rescueth and worketh signs and wonders. So Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian. He had a wise and humble spirit, was beloved by the king, could answer visions and interpret dreams, and was of the king's seed as shown in chapter one. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, made king over the realm of the Chaldeans, Daniel understood by the books the seventy years of the desolations of Jerusalem spoken to Jeremiah. This is the same Darius dealt with when the Persians and Medes were shown in chapters 7 and 8.

Daniel set his face unto the Most High to seek him by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes, confessing that the people had sinned, committed iniquity, done wickedly, and rebelled, departing from his precepts and judgments. They had not hearkened unto the prophets who spake in his name to their kings, princes, fathers, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to the Most High, but confusion of faces to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, near and far off, driven through all the countries because of their trespasses. Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned. -

All Israel transgressed the law by departing, so the curse was poured upon them and the oath written in the law of Moses, because they had sinned against him. The oath that was written is [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), verses 1 through 68. -

Daniel appealed to the Most High who brought his people out of Egypt with a mighty hand, confessing they had sinned and done wickedly, and asking that his anger and fury be turned away from his city Jerusalem, his holy mountain. He pleaded for the Most High to hear, forgive, hearken, and do, not for their righteousness but for his great mercies, since the city and the people are called by his name.

While Daniel was speaking, praying, and confessing his sin and the sin of his people Israel, the man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision, was caused to fly swiftly and touched him about the time of the evening oblation. Gabriel came to give him skill and understanding, for at the beginning of his supplications the commandment came forth, and Daniel was greatly beloved.

Seventy weeks are determined upon the people and the holy city to finish the transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up the vision, and anoint the most Holy. From the going forth of the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem unto Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks and threescore and two weeks, the street built again even in troublous times. After threescore and two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for himself, and the people of the prince that shall come destroy the city and the sanctuary. He confirms the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week causes the sacrifice and oblation to cease. Daniel was given the four beasts first, then this further vision of the seventy weeks by Gabriel in the midst of his prayer and supplications. The bishop's class on the seventy weeks opens this up in full.

Certain of the elders of Israel came and sat before Ezekiel, and the word of the Lord said these men have set up their idols in their hearts, setting up something above God, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. The Most High asks whether He should be inquired of at all by them. Every man of the house of Israel that sets up his idols in his heart and comes to the prophet, the Lord will answer according to the multitude of his idols, that He may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from Him through their idols and spiritual idolatry.

The Most High tells the house of Israel to repent, come back to His laws, and turn themselves from their idols and away from all their abominations. Every one of the house of Israel, or the stranger that sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from Him and sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet to inquire, the Lord will answer by Himself and set His face against that man. He will make him a sign and a proverb, meaning a curse, and cut him off from the midst of His people as an example, that they may know He is the Lord.

If a prophet is deceived when he has spoken a thing, the Lord Himself has deceived that prophet; do not try to deceive yourself in this truth, and when we get counsel we should take it and keep it moving. He will stretch out His hand upon that prophet and destroy him from the midst of His people Israel, and both shall bear the punishment of their iniquity. This is so the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God. -

The word of the Lord came saying that when a land sins by trespassing grievously, He will stretch out His hand upon it, break the staff of its bread, and send famine to cut off man and beast. Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness. No one can save anyone else; it does not matter who you are or what your status is in Israel, you have to save yourself by your own righteousness.

If He causes noisome beasts to pass through the land and spoil it so that it is desolate and no man may pass through, this is one of His judgments. Though these three men were in it, as the Lord lives they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered by their righteousness, but the land shall be desolate.

If He brings a sword upon that land to cut off man and beast, though these three men were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters. They only shall deliver themselves by their righteousness.

If He sends a pestilence into the land and pours out His fury upon it in blood to cut off man and beast, though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter. They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness; everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling, delivering their own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments. -

How much more when the Most High sends His four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, the famine, the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off man and beast; and these are not just for back then but for today. Behold, a remnant shall be left, both sons and daughters, that shall be brought forth unto you, and you shall see their ways and their doings. You shall be comforted concerning the evil the Most High brought upon Jerusalem when you see their ways, and you shall know He has not done without cause all that He has done in it. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

[Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11) tells you what you can and cannot eat. Among all the beasts of the earth, ye shall eat whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud. A cloven hoof is a hoof split into two toes; mammals with this hoof include cattle, deer, antelopes, gazelles, goats, and sheep. Chewing the cud means the animal has more than one stomach: it chews its food, brings it back up into its mouth to be chewed again, and then digests it through another stomach.

Both marks must be present. There are animals that chew the cud and animals that divide the hoof but do not have both; those are unclean. The camel cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof: you cannot eat camel. The coney is the pika, a small mountain dwelling mammal that resembles its close relative the rabbit, found at heights among the highest of any mammal. The scriptures already had it right: the rocks are a refuge for the conies, and the conies, a feeble folk, make their houses in the rocks. You cannot eat coney, and the hare likewise is unclean. The swine has only the one mark: he divideth the hoof and is clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean unto you. You cannot eat pork; leave it alone. Their carcase shall ye not touch sits inside the dietary law: it goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with the mouth. It does not mean a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with the hands; the tabernacle itself had to be built by hand with badgers' skins.

Of all that are in the waters, ye shall eat whatsoever hath fins and scales; whatever has not fins and scales is an abomination. No shrimp, no crab, no lobster, no bottom dwellers. The Most High gave an excellent dietary law: high blood pressure and the like come from eating shellfish. He made these animals and knows what they do; if you eat what he allowed you will be fine. It is simple: if it does not have both fins and scales, leave it alone. A fish must have both scales and fins. Tilapia has scales and fins, so it may be eaten if you want it; sardines do not show both, so it looks like sardines are a no.

These are the fowls in abomination that shall not be eaten: the eagle, the ossifrage, the osprey, the vulture and the kite after his kind, every raven after his kind, the owl, the nighthawk, the cuckow, the hawk, the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl, the swan, the pelican, the gier eagle, the stork, the heron after her kind, the lapwing, and the bat. Look these up. The ossifrage, the bone breaker, is an older name for the bearded vulture, a scavenger famous for dropping bones on rocks to crack them open. The osprey is the seahawk or fishhawk, a fish eating bird of prey. The kite is a bird of prey in the family of the eagle. What is interesting is that all of these are scavengers and hunters; even in the waters the Most High did not want you to have the scavengers, and no shark, a hunter. He gave you this diet because he made these animals and knows what they do. After his kind: when the Most High made one, he made many of them, so the rule covers the whole family. On duck: the swan's closest relatives include the geese and ducks. The swan is unclean, and duck falls in the family of the swan, so you cannot eat duck; they are related, and it is the same thing.

All fowls that creep, going upon all four, are an abomination, yet those which have legs above their feet to leap withal upon the earth may be eaten: the locust, the bald locust, the beetle, and the grasshopper after his kind. You can eat locusts; John the Baptist ate locusts.

The carcases of every beast which divideth the hoof and is not clovenfooted nor cheweth the cud are unclean; whoever touches them is unclean until the even, and whoever bears the carcase washes his clothes. Whatsoever goeth upon his paws, among all manner of beasts that go on all four, is unclean: you cannot eat mountain lion, tiger, cougar, gorilla, dog, or cat; they have paws and walk on all fours.

These creeping things are unclean: the weasel, the mouse, the tortoise after his kind, the ferret, the chameleon, the lizard, the snail, and the mole. You cannot eat tortoise. If you find a dead mouse in your house, do not touch it: sweep it into a bag and throw it out. Whatever vessel one of them falls into when dead is unclean until the even and must be put into water; if it falls into one of your pots, clean that pot out and cook nothing in it until the even. An earthen vessel it falls into is broken and thrown out, and ovens and ranges for pots are broken down. If any part of their carcase falls on sowing seed which is to be sown, the seed is clean; but if water be put upon the seed and the carcase fall thereon, it is unclean and no good.

Even of a beast which ye may eat, if it die of itself, he that toucheth, eateth of, or beareth the carcase is unclean until the even and washes his clothes. Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth is an abomination: whatsoever goeth upon the belly, whatsoever goeth upon all four, and whatsoever hath more feet. You cannot eat centipedes and millipedes.

Sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy, for I am holy: for I am the Lord that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. This is the law of the beast and of the fowl and of every living creature that moveth in the waters and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth; the Most High explained everything and then summed it all up, to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten. Do not confuse yourself with [1 Timothy 4:4](/bible/1-timothy/4#v4), that you can eat whatever you want. Every creature is good and nothing to be refused if it be received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the word of God; so find what the word of God sanctified, and that is the law of the beast in [Leviticus 11](/bible/leviticus/11). What is sanctified is what he already made clean. The law perisheth not, but remaineth in his force; that law did not change at all. Do not let anybody confuse you, especially if you are new in the truth: eat what the Most High instructed you to eat.

verses.text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Now God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs.

And the prince of the eunuchs said unto Daniel, I fear my lord the king, who hath appointed your meat and your drink: for why should he see your faces worse liking than the children which are of your sort? then shall ye make me endanger my head to the king.
Then said Daniel to Melzar, whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days; and let them give us pulse to eat, and water to drink.
Then let our countenances be looked upon before thee, and the countenance of the children that eat of the portion of the king’s meat: and as thou seest, deal with thy servants.
So he consented to them in this matter, and proved them ten days.
And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king’s meat.
Thus Melzar took away the portion of their meat, and the wine that they should drink; and gave them pulse.
As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
Now at the end of the days that the king had said he should bring them in, then the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king communed with them; and among them all was found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: therefore stood they before the king.
And in all matters of wisdom and understanding, that the king enquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers that were in all his realm.
And Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus.

Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Then said these men, We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Then these men assembled, and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.
Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting: neither were instruments of musick brought before him: and his sleep went from him.
Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste unto the den of lions.

And when he came to the den, he cried with a lamentable voice unto Daniel: and the king spake and said to Daniel, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is thy God, whom thou servest continually, able to deliver thee from the lions?
Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
Then king Darius wrote unto all people, nations, and languages, that dwell in all the earth; Peace be multiplied unto you.

I make a decree, That in every dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God, and stedfast for ever, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed, and his dominion shall be even unto the end.
He delivereth and rescueth, and he worketh signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who hath delivered Daniel from the power of the lions.
So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
And whiles I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the Lord my God for the holy mountain of my God;
Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation.
And he informed me, and talked with me, and said, O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding.
At the beginning of thy supplications the commandment came forth, and I am come to shew thee; for thou art greatly beloved: therefore understand the matter, and consider the vision.
Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord God.
This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth:
To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.

Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
Then king Darius wrote unto all people, nations, and languages, that dwell in all the earth; Peace be multiplied unto you.

I make a decree, That in every dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God, and stedfast for ever, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed, and his dominion shall be even unto the end.
He delivereth and rescueth, and he worketh signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who hath delivered Daniel from the power of the lions.
So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
And whiles I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and presenting my supplication before the Lord my God for the holy mountain of my God;
Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation.
And he informed me, and talked with me, and said, O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding.
At the beginning of thy supplications the commandment came forth, and I am come to shew thee; for thou art greatly beloved: therefore understand the matter, and consider the vision.
Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord God.
This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth:
To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.
